rows.en: To the classroom to drop off my things.

ghs.en: I drop off my bags in the classroom.

rows.jp: 来ていると思ったのに。

ghs.en: But I thought she was coming.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the speaker expected the person already to be present or to have come; the progressive English changes that state.

rows.en: Her usual place by the window.

rows.jp: そこにお嬢様の姿はない。
rows.en: No sign of the young lady there.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese expresses a premonitory unease; the English is malformed and weakens the bodily apprehension.

rows.jp: いつもと違う行動を取らないでくれ。
rows.en: Don't do anything out of the ordinary.

ghs.en: Never take actions different from the always.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks the person not to act differently from usual; the English phrase 'different from the always' is not grammatical English.

highlights.text: Never take actions different from the always.

rows.en: A thought almost like a prayer.

ghs.en: A thought that resembled a wish.

rows.jp: ズタ袋を置いて、学校を彷徨う。
rows.en: I set down my gunny sack and roam the school.

ghs.en: Having laid the carryall bag, I go roam about the school.

rows.jp: はじまって三日目の『いつも』。
rows.en: “Usual,” only three days into its existence.

ghs.en: The beginning of the third day of The Always.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese frames this as the third day of a newly established routine; the English instead calls it the beginning of the third day of an entity named 'The Always.'

highlights.text: The beginning of the third day of The Always.

rows.jp: だけどそれは、がらんどうで満たされていて。
rows.en: And yet it was filled with emptiness...
